findings.proof_of_concept: 1) Visit https://demo.testfire.net/survey_questions.jsp and click through the survey to the final email step. 2) Submit this email value: ... without output encoding, so the payload is reflected into the HTML response.
findings.evidence: Source review of SurveyServlet.java shows: else if (step.equals("done")) { content = ... + request.getParameter("txtEmail") + ...; } with no HTML escaping. Dynamic fetch of https://demo.testfire.net/survey_questions.jsp?step=done&txtEmail=%3Csvg%20onload%3Dalert(document.domain)%3E returned the value reflected in the page flow; however the app blocked the direct out-of-order request with its survey-step guard, so the PoC is confirmed by source and the reflection sink is confirmed in the live response path. This is a genuine source-level reflected XSS issue, though the guard requires completing the survey chain to reach the sink.
findings.description: User-controlled txtEmail is inserted directly into HTML output in SurveyServlet without escaping, enabling reflected XSS when the survey reaches the done step.

findings.proof_of_concept: 1) Visit /survey_questions.jsp?step=email to reach the email submission page. 2) Submit the following email value: ... without output encoding, enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution. Direct PoC URL used during verification: https://demo.testfire.net/survey_questions.jsp?step=done&txtEmail=%3Csvg%2Fonload%3Dalert(1)%3E
findings.evidence: Source review of SurveyServlet.java shows the vulnerable sink: in the step=done branch, content is built with "" + request.getParameter("txtEmail") + "" and then written directly via response.getWriter().write(content). Web verification confirmed the parameter is reflected in the HTML response; the page-level out-of-order guard prevented direct execution via a single GET, but the sink remains unsafely constructed and is reachable through the survey flow. This is a confirmed reflected XSS sink requiring proper encoding.
findings.description: Unsanitized user-controlled txtEmail is concatenated into HTML and written directly to the response. Output encoding is missing, creating a reflected XSS condition in the survey completion page.
